title: Bhimsen and Fever
summary: Proud, mighty Bhimsen challenges a stranger called Fever to a wrestling match. When his family helps him test a clever plan, he learns that some opponents cannot be beaten by strength alone.
from: Folktale, Chhattisgarh (from Twente, Folk Tales of Chhattisgarh India)
levelReason: The supplied text uses mostly plain, concrete wording with some less common words (encountered, astonishment, withstand, recognising). Sentences average about 10 words, joined with simple connectors, and the ending states the lesson directly. That is too rich for Level 1 but not as layered or atmospheric as Level 3, so it matches Level 2.

en: Long ago, Bhimsen was hurrying home through a forest. People also called him Baiha Bajrangi.
He walked along the jungle path. A strange man came toward him from the other side.
“Who are you?” asked Bhimsen. “I am Fever,” said the stranger.
Bhimsen was very strong. He was never afraid. He thought nobody could beat him. “Do you want to wrestle with me?” he asked.
Fever said yes. “Why not, Bhimsen?” he said. “Then let us start!” said Bhimsen.
But Fever had an idea. “Let us meet here again after eight days.” Bhimsen agreed. Then they went their own ways.
Bhimsen reached home. He told his family about the wrestling match. They were scared. “You cannot beat Fever!” they said.
Bhimsen was surprised. “Then what should I do?” he asked.
His family thought hard. Then they shared a clever plan. “On that day, make a stone statue of yourself. Put it at the meeting place. Hide close by and watch.”
Bhimsen did as they said. After eight days, he put a stone statue of himself at the spot. Then he hid nearby.
Soon Fever came. He saw the stone statue. He went right inside it. The statue broke into tiny bits, like sand!
Bhimsen was amazed. Fever was stronger than any muscle. Even hard stone could not stand against him.
From that day, Bhimsen never challenged Fever again. He learned something important. Strength and courage cannot beat every enemy. Wise people know where their power ends.
Moral: Think before you take on a challenge. Strength alone cannot solve every problem.
hi: बहुत समय पहले की बात है। भीमसेन जंगल से होकर जल्दी-जल्दी घर जा रहा था। लोग उसे बैहा बजरंगी भी कहते थे।
वह जंगल की पगडंडी पर चल रहा था। तभी सामने से एक अजीब आदमी आया।
“तुम कौन हो?” भीमसेन ने पूछा। “मैं बुखार हूँ,” अजनबी ने कहा।
भीमसेन बहुत ताकतवर था। उसे किसी से डर नहीं लगता था। वह सोचता था कि उसे कोई हरा नहीं सकता। उसने कहा, “क्या तुम मुझसे कुश्ती लड़ोगे?”
बुखार मान गया। “क्यों नहीं, भीमसेन?” उसने कहा। “तो चलो, शुरू करें!” भीमसेन बोला।
पर बुखार ने कहा, “आठ दिन बाद हम यहीं फिर मिलेंगे।” भीमसेन मान गया। फिर दोनों अपने-अपने रास्ते चले गए।
भीमसेन घर पहुँचा। उसने परिवार को कुश्ती के बारे में बताया। वे घबरा गए। “तुम बुखार को नहीं हरा सकते!” उन्होंने कहा।
भीमसेन हैरान हो गया। उसने पूछा, “तो मैं क्या करूँ?”
परिवार ने खूब सोचा। फिर उन्होंने एक चतुर उपाय बताया। “उस दिन अपनी एक पत्थर की मूर्ति बनाओ। उसे मिलने की जगह पर रख दो। पास में छिप जाओ और देखो।”
भीमसेन ने वैसा ही किया। आठ दिन बाद उसने अपनी पत्थर की मूर्ति उस जगह रखी। फिर वह पास में छिप गया।
जल्दी ही बुखार आ गया। उसने पत्थर की मूर्ति देखी। वह उसके अंदर घुस गया। मूर्ति टूटकर रेत की तरह छोटे-छोटे टुकड़े हो गई!
भीमसेन दंग रह गया। बुखार की ताकत किसी भी पहलवानी से बड़ी थी। ठोस पत्थर भी उसके सामने नहीं टिक सका।
उस दिन के बाद भीमसेन ने बुखार को फिर कभी चुनौती नहीं दी। उसने एक ज़रूरी बात सीखी। ताकत और हिम्मत से हर दुश्मन नहीं हारता। समझदार लोग जानते हैं कि उनकी ताकत की हद कहाँ तक है।
सीख: किसी चुनौती को लेने से पहले सोचो। अकेली ताकत हर मुश्किल को हल नहीं कर सकती।

en: Once upon a time, Bhimsen, also known as Baiha Bajrangi, was hurrying home through a forest.
As he walked along the jungle path, he encountered a strange man approaching from the opposite direction.
“Who are you?” Bhimsen asked. “I am Fever,” replied the stranger.
Bhimsen was a powerful and fearless man. He believed that there was no opponent he could not defeat. Looking at the stranger, he confidently challenged him. “Would you like to wrestle with me?”
Fever accepted the challenge. “Why should I not wrestle with you, Bhimsen?” he replied. “Then let us begin!” said Bhimsen.
But Fever suggested that they meet again after eight days at the same spot. Bhimsen agreed, and the two went their separate ways.
When Bhimsen reached home, he proudly told his family about the wrestling match he had arranged. His family members were alarmed. “You cannot defeat Fever,” they warned him.
Bhimsen was surprised. “What should I do, then?” he asked.
His family thought carefully and suggested a clever plan. “On the appointed day, make a stone statue of yourself and place it at the meeting spot. Hide nearby and watch what happens.”
Bhimsen followed their advice. Eight days later, he placed a stone image of himself at the agreed location and hid nearby.
Soon, Fever arrived. Seeing the stone figure, Fever approached it and entered the image. At once, the statue shattered into tiny pieces, crumbling like sand.
Bhimsen watched in astonishment. He realised that Fever possessed a power far greater than physical strength. Even a solid stone statue could not withstand it.

From that day onwards, Bhimsen decided never to challenge Fever again. He understood that not every opponent could be defeated through strength and courage. Sometimes, wisdom meant recognising the limits of one's own power.
Moral: Think carefully before taking on a challenge. Strength alone cannot overcome every difficulty.

भीमसेन बहुत ताकतवर और निडर था। उसे विश्वास था कि दुनिया में ऐसा कोई प्रतिद्वंद्वी नहीं जिसे वह हरा न सके। अजनबी को देखकर उसने पूरे भरोसे के साथ ललकारा, “क्या तुम मुझसे कुश्ती लड़ना चाहोगे?”

लेकिन बुखार ने सुझाव दिया कि वे आठ दिन बाद इसी जगह फिर मिलें। भीमसेन मान गया और दोनों अपने-अपने रास्ते चले गए।
घर पहुँचकर भीमसेन ने बड़े गर्व से अपने परिवार को उस कुश्ती के बारे में बताया जो उसने तय की थी। परिवार के लोग घबरा गए। “तुम बुखार को नहीं हरा सकते,” उन्होंने उसे चेताया।
भीमसेन हैरान रह गया। “तो फिर मुझे क्या करना चाहिए?” उसने पूछा।
परिवार ने ध्यान से सोचा और एक चतुर उपाय सुझाया। “तय दिन पर अपनी एक पत्थर की मूर्ति बनाकर मिलने की जगह पर रख दो। पास में कहीं छिप जाओ और देखो कि क्या होता है।”
भीमसेन ने उनकी सलाह मानी। आठ दिन बाद उसने अपनी पत्थर की मूर्ति तय जगह पर रखी और पास में छिप गया।

उस दिन के बाद भीमसेन ने तय किया कि वह बुखार को फिर कभी चुनौती नहीं देगा। वह समझ गया कि हर प्रतिद्वंद्वी को ताकत और साहस से नहीं हराया जा सकता। कभी-कभी समझदारी का मतलब अपनी शक्ति की सीमा को पहचानना होता है।
सीख: चुनौती स्वीकार करने से पहले ध्यान से सोचो। अकेली ताकत हर कठिनाई को पार नहीं कर सकती।

vocab.en: the person you compete or fight against
knowing and accepting that something is true

questions.q: Why did Bhimsen challenge a stranger to wrestle? What did he believe about himself?
Why did Bhimsen's family become alarmed when he told them about the match?
Bhimsen hid and watched instead of just trusting his family. What did that choice help him learn?
The story says Fever had a power greater than physical strength. What kind of power do you think that means?
How did Bhimsen change after the statue crumbled? Do you think this made him weaker or wiser? Explain.

en: Once upon a time, Bhimsen, whom people also called Baiha Bajrangi, was hurrying homeward through a deep forest, his heavy footsteps echoing along the path.
Somewhere along the winding jungle trail, he came face to face with a stranger walking toward him from the opposite direction, someone he had never seen before.
“Who are you?” Bhimsen demanded. “I am Fever,” the stranger answered calmly.

Bhimsen was a man of immense strength and no fear, convinced that no opponent existed whom he could not defeat. Studying the stranger with confidence, he issued a challenge: “Would you care to wrestle with me?”
Fever accepted without hesitation. “Why should I refuse to wrestle with you, Bhimsen?” he replied. “Then let the contest begin!” declared Bhimsen.
Yet Fever proposed that they meet again at the very same spot after eight days. Bhimsen consented, and the two parted, each going his own way.
Arriving home, Bhimsen proudly told his family about the match he had arranged, but their faces filled with alarm. “You cannot defeat Fever,” they warned him gravely.
Bhimsen was taken aback. “What am I to do, then?” he asked.

After thinking it over carefully, his family offered a clever plan. “On the appointed day, make a stone statue of yourself and place it at the meeting spot. Then hide close by and watch what happens.”
Bhimsen followed their advice. When the eighth day came, he placed a stone likeness of himself at the agreed place and concealed himself nearby, waiting.
Before long, Fever arrived. Seeing the stone figure, he walked up to it and entered the image. At that very instant, the statue burst apart and crumbled into tiny pieces, like sand.
Bhimsen watched in stunned astonishment. He understood that Fever held a power far beyond mere physical strength, one that even solid stone could not endure.

From that day on, Bhimsen resolved never to challenge Fever again. He had learned that not every opponent can be conquered by strength and courage, and that true wisdom sometimes lies in recognising the limits of one's own power.
Moral: Think carefully before taking on a challenge, for strength alone cannot overcome every difficulty.
hi: बहुत पुरानी बात है। भीमसेन, जिसे लोग बैहा बजरंगी भी कहते थे, घने जंगल के बीच से घर की ओर बढ़ा चला जा रहा था, और उसके भारी कदमों की धमक पगडंडी पर गूँज रही थी।
जंगल की टेढ़ी-मेढ़ी राह पर कहीं आगे चलते हुए अचानक उसका सामना एक अनजान आदमी से हुआ, जो सामने से चला आ रहा था। उसे भीमसेन ने पहले कभी नहीं देखा था।
“कौन हो तुम?” भीमसेन ने रौब से पूछा। “मैं बुखार हूँ,” अजनबी ने शांत स्वर में उत्तर दिया।

भीमसेन में अपार बल था और किसी बात का डर नहीं था। उसे पक्का यक़ीन था कि ऐसा कोई प्रतिद्वंद्वी बना ही नहीं जिसे वह हरा न सके। अजनबी को भरोसे से परखते हुए उसने ललकारा, “क्या तुम मुझसे कुश्ती लड़ना पसंद करोगे?”
बुखार ने बिना झिझके चुनौती मान ली। “भीमसेन, मैं तुमसे कुश्ती लड़ने से इनकार क्यों करूँ?” उसने कहा। “तो फिर मुक़ाबला शुरू हो!” भीमसेन ने घोषणा की।
फिर भी बुखार ने प्रस्ताव रखा कि वे आठ दिन बाद ठीक इसी जगह दोबारा मिलें। भीमसेन राज़ी हो गया और दोनों अपनी-अपनी राह चल पड़े।
घर लौटकर भीमसेन ने बड़े गर्व से परिवार को उस कुश्ती के बारे में बताया जो उसने तय की थी, पर सबके चेहरे डर से भर उठे। “तुम बुखार को नहीं हरा सकते,” उन्होंने गंभीरता से उसे चेताया।
भीमसेन चकित रह गया। “तो फिर मैं क्या करूँ?” उसने पूछा।
परिवार ने बहुत सोच-विचार किया और एक चतुर उपाय सुझाया। “तय दिन पर अपनी एक पत्थर की मूर्ति बनाकर उसे मिलने की जगह पर रख दो। फिर पास में छिप जाओ और देखो कि क्या होता है।”
भीमसेन ने उनकी सलाह मान ली। आठवाँ दिन आया तो उसने अपनी पत्थर की प्रतिमा तय जगह पर रखी और पास में छिपकर इंतज़ार करने लगा।
कुछ ही देर में बुखार आ पहुँचा। पत्थर की आकृति को देखकर वह उसकी ओर बढ़ा और उसके भीतर समा गया। उसी क्षण मूर्ति चटककर बिखर गई और रेत की तरह नन्हे-नन्हे टुकड़ों में ढह गई।
भीमसेन स्तब्ध होकर आश्चर्य से देखता रह गया। उसे समझ आ गया कि बुखार के पास ऐसी शक्ति है जो केवल शारीरिक बल से कहीं आगे है, जिसे ठोस पत्थर भी नहीं सह सका।

उस दिन के बाद भीमसेन ने ठान लिया कि वह बुखार को फिर कभी चुनौती नहीं देगा। उसने जान लिया था कि हर प्रतिद्वंद्वी को ताकत और साहस से नहीं जीता जा सकता, और सच्ची समझदारी कभी-कभी अपनी शक्ति की सीमाओं को पहचानने में होती है।
सीख: किसी चुनौती को स्वीकार करने से पहले खूब सोच-विचार करो, क्योंकि अकेली ताकत हर कठिनाई पर विजय नहीं पा सकती।

vocab.en: a sudden feeling of fear or worry
a copy that looks just like someone
hid so as not to be seen
to survive something hard without giving way

questions.q: Bhimsen challenged a stranger without knowing anything about him. Was this fair or wise? What should a person find out before accepting or giving a challenge?
Imagine how Bhimsen's family felt when he came home proud of the match. Why might they have chosen to give him a plan instead of simply forbidding him?
The story ends by saying wisdom can mean recognising the limits of one's power. Do you think accepting limits is a sign of weakness or of strength? Why?
Fever is shown here as a character, someone who can walk, speak and make a plan. Why might a community tell a story that turns an illness into a person?
What are some challenges today that cannot be solved by strength or confidence alone? How might people face them wisely?

scenes.p: A forest path in Chhattisgarh in soft morning light, tall sal trees and dappled shade. Bhimsen, a tall, broad-shouldered man with dark skin, a topknot, a plain cotton dhoti and a heavy walking staff, stops on the path facing Fever, a thin pale stranger in a grey-green shawl with a faint shimmer of heat haze around him. They look at each other with curiosity. Mood: calm but a little mysterious. Storybook illustration, same character looks in every scene.

Bhimsen stands proudly with his chest out and one hand pointing, challenging Fever to wrestle. Fever, thin and pale in the grey-green shawl with a faint heat shimmer, calmly raises a hand to agree. Same forest path, sal trees, light filtering through leaves. Mood: confident and playful, no violence.

A village home courtyard in Chhattisgarh with a mud-walled house, a tulsi plant and a clay pot. Bhimsen, tall with a topknot and cotton dhoti, speaks proudly while his mother, wife and younger brother, in simple cotton saris and dhotis, look worried and alarmed. Warm afternoon light. Mood: worry rising.

Inside the courtyard, the family sits close to Bhimsen, thinking hard; the mother holds up a finger explaining the idea while Bhimsen listens surprised. A rough block of grey stone and a chisel lie nearby, hinting at a statue. Evening lamp light, warm colours. Mood: thoughtful, hopeful.

At the meeting spot on the forest path, a life-sized grey stone statue of Bhimsen stands. Fever, thin and pale in the grey-green shawl, touches it and heat haze ripples, the statue cracking and crumbling into sand, shown in a gentle, non-scary way. Bhimsen peeks out from behind a large tree trunk, eyes wide. Mood: astonishing and quiet.

Bhimsen sits on a rock beside a small heap of sand where the statue stood, hand on chin, thoughtful and humbled, the forest quiet around him with golden late-afternoon light. His walking staff rests beside him. Mood: calm, reflective, hopeful.

artStyle.note: Bastar wall painting, made by communities such as the Gond, Halba and Bhatra, traditionally uses a limited palette of white lime, red ochre, charcoal black and yellow clay, with strongly outlined, flat figures and geometric borders, and Bhimadeo appears among its subjects. We could not confirm that this story belongs to those communities, so use this only as gentle inspiration for colour and line: warm earth tones, bold outlines, simple geometric borders. Do not label the images as Bastar art.

imagine: Imagine you are hiding behind the tree and watching the stone statue crumble. What do you see, hear and feel? What would you say to Bhimsen when he comes out?
create: Draw the meeting spot in the forest, or write a short new diary page from Bhimsen on the night after the statue crumbled, saying what he now knows.

about.where: Chhattisgarh is a state in central India, with many forests and many rivers. This story is listed as a folktale of Chhattisgarh, in a book of tales published in 1938.
about.community: The sources we have do not say which community first told this version, so we are not guessing. This is one version from one source, and other tellers may tell it differently.
about.tradition: Bhimsen is the Chhattisgarhi form of the name of Bhima, the strong second brother of the Pandavas in the Mahabharata. In Chhattisgarh, the Mahabharata is also told through Pandavani, a folk singing style in which a singer tells an episode with a tambura and Bhima is often the hero.
about.shared: Stories where a boaster learns his limits are found in many places. Here the lesson is a gentle one: even someone as strong as Bhima can learn to stop and think.
about.matters: The story shows that wisdom and caution can matter as much as strength. It also shows that listening to family and testing a plan before acting can help.
